raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Refs #39604. `BlockRemoved` says which blocks left a tier but not why, so a consumer cannot tell capacity eviction from a demotion that left the content readable in a lower tier. That is the difference between a cache miss meaning pressure and a miss that is still servable, and today it has to be inferred from timing and unrelated scheduler state.

The issue asks for the event semantics to be settled before implementation, so the first half of this description is what the call sites actually say. The vocabulary below is derived from them, not proposed from outside, and I am happy to rename any of it.

### What the removal paths actually are

#40313 removed the SWA and Mamba radix caches and #40787 removed HiRadixCache while this PR was open, so after merging `main` there are 5 `kv_events.record_remove(...)` call sites, in `radix_cache` and `unified_tree_core`. Grouped by what is true of the content afterwards:

| cause | call sites | after the event, the content is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| capacity eviction | `radix_cache.evict`, `unified_tree_core._release_all_component_layers`, `unified_tree_core._evict_host_leaf` | gone |
| demotion | `unified_tree_core._demote` | on host |
| duplicate reclaim | `unified_tree_core._release_full_host_duplicate` | still on device |

Three of the five collapse to one reason. The Rust tree core, the default backend, has the same paths and emits the same reasons: `release_all_component_layers_` and `evict_host_leaf_` (evicted), `demote_` (demoted), `release_coexisting_host_value_` (duplicate reclaim).

**Two of the four candidate values in the issue have no emitting call site.** `request_finished` and `aborted` do not appear, because finishing or aborting a request only drops a lock reference; the blocks stay in the tree until one of the causes above removes them. Emitting them would mean inventing removals that do not happen, so this PR leaves them out. `AllBlocksCleared` stays the representation of an explicit global clear, as the issue suggests.

### Compatibility

`KVCacheEvent` is a tagged msgpack **map** with `omit_defaults=True`. Only `EventBatch` is `array_like`, and it is untouched. So an optional field left unset is absent from the payload, and a consumer that does not know the key never sees it. `BlockStored` already gained `cache_salt` and `session_id` this way.

The in-repo Rust consumer confirms it rather than assumes it. `sgl-kv-indexer`'s bridge decodes `BlockRemoved` by looking up the keys it routes on and ignores the rest, and the `KvCacheEvent` doc comment in the router's `wire` module already says exactly that about `BlockStored`: "Keys the gateway does not route on (`cache_salt`, `session_id`) are ignored." Nothing in the KV-event path uses `deny_unknown_fields`; the only uses of it in the router are on config and tokenize types. No Rust change is needed, and none is included.

## Modifications

```python
class BlockRemoved(KVCacheEvent):
    block_hashes: list[int]
    medium: Optional[str] = None
    reason: Optional[str] = None
```

- `RemovalReason(str, enum.Enum)` next to `StorageMedium`, mirroring how `medium` is already typed: a documented vocabulary, carried on the wire as a plain string. Values: `evicted`, `demoted`, `duplicate_reclaimed`.
- The wire default is `None`, not `evicted`. "Not stated" and "evicted" are different claims, and an unset field keeps today's byte shape.
- `KVCacheEventRecorder.record_remove` takes `reason` as a keyword defaulting to `RemovalReason.EVICTED`, the way `medium` already defaults to `StorageMedium.GPU`. Only the three non-eviction sites pass anything, which keeps the diff to the paths whose meaning actually differs.
- The coalescing predicate now compares `reason` as well as `medium` (point 4 of the issue). Merging removals with different causes would report demoted blocks as evicted.
- Rust tree core: `KvCacheEvent::BlockRemoved` carries a `RemovalReason` (`as_str()` gives the Python values), set at the four `record_remove_event_` sites. `enqueue_kv_event_` coalesces removals only when the reason matches as well. The binding appends the reason to the `block_removed` tuple, so the existing indices stay where they are, and `rust_tree_core/adapter.py` passes it to `BlockRemoved`.

Deliberately not included: `cache_salt` on `BlockRemoved` (question 3 in the issue). It is a separate change with its own symmetry argument, and folding it in here would blur what this PR is asking to agree.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable; no model outputs or kernels are touched.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The added work per removal is one keyword argument and one extra `==` in the coalescing predicate.

## Unit tests

Extended the two files that already own this surface, `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_kv_events.py` (wire contract) and `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_unit.py` (recorder and coalescing).

| test | what it stops |
| --- | --- |
| an old consumer decodes an event carrying each reason | the field breaking existing subscribers |
| a new consumer reads an event emitted without one, and sees `None` | a missing reason being read as `evicted` |
| omitting the reason leaves exactly `{type, block_hashes, medium}` | the wire shape changing for emitters that state nothing |
| `reason` is a named field, and survives a mixed batch | the value being dropped in transit |
| removals with different reasons do not coalesce | the merge that would relabel demotions as evictions |
| removals with the same reason still coalesce | the guard defeating the batching it sits in |
| `record_remove` defaults to `evicted` and carries an explicit reason | the recorder silently dropping the argument |

Run on CPU, no accelerator:

```
test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_kv_events.py              22 passed, 25 subtests passed
test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_unit.py            5 passed (TestKVCacheEventQueue)
```

On current `main`, `test_kv_events.py` is 17 passed / 22 subtests (numbers after merging `main`, which added `TestReplay`).

Rust tree core (`cargo test --no-default-features` for `sglang-radix-tree`, as in `pr-test-rust-workspace.yml`): 945 passed, 1 ignored. New: `demotion_emits_a_demoted_gpu_block_removed`, `reclaiming_a_host_duplicate_emits_a_duplicate_reclaimed_cpu_block_removed` and `block_removed_events_with_different_reasons_stay_separate`; all three fail when the sites pass `Evicted` again and the coalescing ignores the reason. The existing event tests now state `RemovalReason::Evicted` for their eviction paths. In `test_rust_tree_core_integration.py` the demote expectation now has `reason=RemovalReason.DEMOTED` and the two eviction expectations `RemovalReason.EVICTED`; that suite needs the built extension, which `torch_build.py` only supports on Linux, so CI runs it and I could not here.

Mutation results, 5 of 5 caught:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| coalescing ignores the reason again | **caught** |
| the recorder stops forwarding the reason | **caught** |
| the recorder default flips to `demoted` | **caught** |
| the wire field defaults to `"evicted"` instead of unset | **caught** |
| `demoted` and `evicted` collapse to one value | **caught** |

The rest of `test_radix_cache_unit.py` fails the same 9 tests on `main` and on this branch, all with `HiCache native hash is only supported on little-endian Linux`. The unified and rust-core suites had the same pass, fail and skip counts on both sides when I last compared them. Their failures are environmental on this machine (the native hash, and CUDA-only paths); I have no GPU here, so the cache-level tests that would exercise the two named call sites end to end are skipped rather than passing. Those two classifications come from reading the call sites, and are the part of this PR most worth a maintainer's eye.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests according to Run and add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

Documentation is unticked because I could not find an existing consumer-facing page describing the KV event schema; the vocabulary is documented on `RemovalReason` itself. Point me at the right page and I will add it.

The call-site table in the description is updated: 5 sites remain, in `radix_cache` and `unified_tree_core`.

@sohom-cs Good catch, thank you. With the Rust core as the default, leaving it out would have made the reason `None` for almost everyone, so I carried it through in this PR (9cd5cb61b7, after merging `main`):

- `KvCacheEvent::BlockRemoved` has a `reason: RemovalReason` (`evicted`, `demoted`, `duplicate_reclaimed`, same strings as the Python enum).
- The four `record_remove_event_` sites pass it the way their Python counterparts do: `release_all_component_layers_` and `evict_host_leaf_` evicted, `demote_` demoted, `release_coexisting_host_value_` duplicate reclaimed.
- `enqueue_kv_event_` only coalesces removals whose reason matches too.
- The binding appends the reason to the `block_removed` tuple (the existing indices stay put), and `adapter.py` builds `BlockRemoved(..., reason=RemovalReason(event[4]))`.

`cargo test --no-default-features` for `sglang-radix-tree`: 945 passed, 1 ignored, including three new tests (demotion, duplicate reclaim, no coalescing across reasons) that fail without the change. I updated the three `BlockRemoved` expectations in `test_rust_tree_core_integration.py` (the demote one to `DEMOTED`, the two evictions to `EVICTED`). That suite needs the built extension, which `torch_build.py` only supports on Linux, so it will run in CI. The description is updated as well.

Use one space between fields and after the colon, with a non-empty title and no leading or trailing whitespace. Examples: "[Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing", "[Feat] qwen3: Add model support", "[Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance".
Edit the title; the check reruns on its own.

The reason is only set in the Python tree core. On main, with the default tree core (`SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND` is `rust`; Python is the fallback), a removal goes through `record_remove_event_` (`rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/unified_tree_core.rs:3713`), which carries the hashes and the medium only, and the adapter turns that tuple into `BlockRemoved(block_hashes=..., medium=...)` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/rust_tree_core/adapter.py:145`). So on that path every event has `reason=None`, including the Rust counterparts of the two paths labelled here, `demote_` and `release_coexisting_host_value_`. Should the reason go through the Rust `KvCacheEvent::BlockRemoved` and the binding tuple in this PR, or should the description name the Rust core as a follow-up?

@@ -267,6 +267,26 @@ class StorageMedium(str, enum.Enum):
     EXTERNAL = "EXTERNAL"  # L4: shared / remote pool (e.g. Mooncake)
 
 
+class RemovalReason(str, enum.Enum):
+    """Why blocks left a storage tier in a ``BlockRemoved`` event.
+
+    These are the causes the cache implementations actually distinguish at the
+    point of removal. The difference that matters to a consumer is whether the
+    content is gone or merely somewhere else: a miss after ``EVICTED`` means
+    capacity pressure, a miss after ``DEMOTED`` is still servable from a lower
+    tier. Request completion and abort are deliberately absent -- finishing a
+    request only drops a lock reference, and the blocks stay cached until one
+    of the causes below removes them.
+    """
+
+    # Capacity pressure. This action kept no copy anywhere else.
+    EVICTED = "evicted"
+    # Freed here because a copy exists in a lower tier (e.g. GPU -> host).
+    DEMOTED = "demoted"
+    # A redundant copy was reclaimed; the block stays cached in a higher tier.
+    DUPLICATE_RECLAIMED = "duplicate_reclaimed"

issue_comments.body: Merged `main`. HiRadixCache (#40787) and the SWA and Mamba radix caches (#40313) were removed in the meantime, so their call sites leave this PR with them; `test_kv_events.py` keeps both `TestReplay` from `main` and the removal-reason tests (22 passed, 25 subtests on CPU). The call-site table in the description is updated: 5 sites remain, in `radix_cache` and `unified_tree_core`.

@sohom-cs Good catch, thank you. With the Rust core as the default, leaving it out would have made the reason `None` for almost everyone, so I carried it through in this PR (9cd5cb61b7, after merging `main`):

- `KvCacheEvent::BlockRemoved` has a `reason: RemovalReason` (`evicted`, `demoted`, `duplicate_reclaimed`, same strings as the Python enum).
- The four `record_remove_event_` sites pass it the way their Python counterparts do: `release_all_component_layers_` and `evict_host_leaf_` evicted, `demote_` demoted, `release_coexisting_host_value_` duplicate reclaimed.
- `enqueue_kv_event_` only coalesces removals whose reason matches too.
- The binding appends the reason to the `block_removed` tuple (the existing indices stay put), and `adapter.py` builds `BlockRemoved(..., reason=RemovalReason(event[4]))`.

`cargo test --no-default-features` for `sglang-radix-tree`: 945 passed, 1 ignored, including three new tests (demotion, duplicate reclaim, no coalescing across reasons) that fail without the change. I updated the three `BlockRemoved` expectations in `test_rust_tree_core_integration.py` (the demote one to `DEMOTED`, the two evictions to `EVICTED`). That suite needs the built extension, which `torch_build.py` only supports on Linux, so it will run in CI. The description is updated as well.

reviews.body:
The reason is only set in the Python tree core. On main, with the default tree core (`SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND` is `rust`; Python is the fallback), a removal goes through `record_remove_event_` (`rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/unified_tree_core.rs:3713`), which carries the hashes and the medium only, and the adapter turns that tuple into `BlockRemoved(block_hashes=..., medium=...)` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/rust_tree_core/adapter.py:145`). So on that path every event has `reason=None`, including the Rust counterparts of the two paths labelled here, `demote_` and `release_coexisting_host_value_`. The new tests exercise the recorder and the wire format, not either core's eviction paths.

Should the reason go through the Rust `KvCacheEvent::BlockRemoved` and the binding tuple in this PR, or should the description name the Rust core as a follow-up?
